Any place of the paper can be linked to: viewer.html#nameddest=thm:small opens the theorem labelled thm:small, viewer.html#page=6 a page; the labels are in the contents below (each entry also has an anchor on this page). The same works with the PDF itself: paper/d5.pdf#nameddest=thm:small.

For a group $G$ let $D_n(G)=G\cap(1+\Delta(G)^n)$ be its integral dimension subgroups and $\gamma_n(G)$ its lower central series. Whether $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for every group is open (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 20.84); for Lie rings the analogous inclusion was recently proved by Ionin, Mikhailov and Petrov, and formally verified in Lean. We approach the group question from several sides. We reduce it, by an elementary argument, to finite metabelian $2$-groups of class three, and analyse which steps of the Lie-ring proof have no group-theoretic counterpart. A computer search shows that a counterexample among finite $2$-groups of class three has order at least $2^{12}$. For $3$-torsion in $D_5/\gamma_5$ we prove $D_5(G)=\gamma_5(G)$ whenever $G/\gamma_2(G)$ is a finite $3$-group with at most one invariant larger than $3$, and, with a computer search, for all $3$-groups of order at most $3^9$. Along the way we give an exact criterion for a $p$-group of type $(d,2,1)$ with elementary abelian $P/\gamma_2(P)$, $p$ odd, to have immediate descendants, and an explicit graded Lie algebra of type $(3,3,1,1)$ over $\mathbb F_p$ with $[L_2,L_2]\ne0$, which shows that the Lie-ring lemma behind our metabelian results needs $\gamma_2/\gamma_3$ to have at most two generators.
